group:paper-mock-liaoning-2024-12-famous.overview: 作者自幼迷恋昆虫，给蚂蚁搭小房子起步，成为微雕艺术家；创作虽艰辛，却让他见到女王、两创吉尼斯纪录。曾被老师看作失败者的他视自闭症为天赋，并到学校与孩子分享。
group:paper-mock-liaoning-2024-12-famous.fullTranslationZh:
我在英国长大，小时候就对昆虫着迷。为了保护它们，我开始用小木片和树叶给蚂蚁搭小房子。母亲看到我的作品后告诉我，我把东西做得越小，名气就会越大。
随着岁月流逝，我的设计越来越复杂。我还用上了许多不同的材料，比如蜘蛛丝。我有时一天连续工作 16 个小时，中间不休息，完成一件雕塑要花上长达三个月的时间。雕刻过程中我得屏住呼吸。这个过程其实并不令人享受——只有完成之后我才能享受它。
我的雕塑带我去了许多不可思议的地方。2012 年，我见到了女王，送给她一顶放在针头上的微型王冠。2013 年，我因创作出世界上最小的手工雕塑获得了第一项吉尼斯世界纪录，那是一辆金摩托，能放进一根被钻空的头发里。2017 年，我用一件人类胎儿雕塑打破了自己的纪录，它的尺寸只有 0.078 毫米 × 0.053 毫米。
我成年后被诊断出患有自闭症。上学时，老师们曾把我当作失败者；如今，我把自闭症看作一份天赋。它推动我做到最好。我在学校为孩子们举办讲习班，与他们分享我的人生和作品，帮助他们创作自己的微型雕像。我们要懂得珍视生活中的小东西。小东西也可以很有力量。

theme.text: 小东西也能有大力量，要懂得珍视生活中的小事物（Small things can also be mighty）。
theme.quote: Small things can also be mighty

completedSourceTexts.text: Growing up as a kid in the U. K., I was fascinated by insects. Wanting to protect them, I started building little houses for ants, using little pieces of wood and leaves. When my mother saw my work, she told me that the smaller I made things, the bigger my name would become.

As the years went by, my designs became more complicated. And I used many different materials, such as spider web threads. I sometimes work for 16 hours on end a day without breaks, and it takes me up to three months to finish a(n) sculpture. I have to hold my breath during the sculpting process. It isn’t actually an enjoyable process – I can only enjoy it once I’ve finished it.

My sculptures have taken me to incredible places. In 2012, I met the queen, giving her a tiny crown on the head of a pin. In 2013, I received my first Guinness World Record for creating the smallest sculpture made by hand, a gold motorbike that fitted inside a drilled out hair. In 2017, I beat my record with a sculpture of a
human fetus(胎儿) that measured 0.078mm by 0.053mm.

I was diagnosed with autism(自闭症) as an adult. In school, my teachers had pointed me out as a failure; now, I see my autism as a gift. It has pushed me to be the best I can be. I hold workshops in schools for children, sharing with them my life and work and helping them create their own miniature figures. We need to appreciate the little things in life. Small things can also be mighty, too.
